title: Request Surface & Compatibility Negotiation Proposal
content:
Purpose and scope

This doc proposes a pragmatic request surface and a capability/compatibility negotiation flow for the serving runtime. It focuses on: (1) a stable, small core request schema, (2) explicit capability negotiation so clients and runtimes can evolve independently, (3) an error-code taxonomy that supports automated fallbacks, and (4) clear guarantees for backward/forward compatibility including deprecation windows. It also covers runtime-side hints for kernel selection, scheduling, and KV cache behavior that are safe to expose in the public API.

Why this is needed
- Past incidents: silent request drops or confusing 4xx/5xx behavior during model rollouts.
- Customers build fallbacks (cheaper model, region failover) but need deterministic signals to decide.
- We must support incremental runtime features (quantized kernels, low-memory execution) without breaking older clients.

Design goals
- Minimal stable core: small number of guaranteed fields that are expected to be accepted forever.
- Capability-based extension: optional features are negotiated explicitly.
- Deterministic fallback signals: machine-readable error codes + policy hints.
- Graceful deprecation: calendarized windows and discoverable change logs.

Core request schema (human-readable explanation)
- client_request_id (string): client-generated idempotency key, recommended for non-idempotent flows.
- protocol_version (string): api surface/semver-like token for negotiation (e.g. "rapi/1.2").
- model (string): model identifier (catalog name).
- model_version (string, optional): explicit pinned model version. If absent, runtime selects default.
- input_type (enum): "text" | "chat" | "tokens".
- input (string or array-of-messages-as-strings): payload matching input_type. For chat, message array is allowed.
- response_format (string, optional): "raw" | "structured/json-schema:<uri>" | "embeddings:<dim>".
- streaming (boolean, optional): client preference for streaming; runtime may downgrade.
- max_tokens (int, optional)
- temperature (float, optional)
- top_p (float, optional)
- stop_sequences (array of strings, optional)
- resource_hints (string[], optional): freeform short hints like ["low-latency", "gpu-memory-conservative"].
- kernel_hint (enum, optional): "prefer_fast_fp16", "prefer_quantized_int8", "prefer_low_memory". This is a soft hint only.
- kv_cache_policy (string, optional): "use_cache" | "bypass_cache" | "populate_only".
- batching_hint_ms (int, optional): preferred batching window in ms; runtime may override.
- latency_slo_ms (int, optional): request-level SLO hint (best-effort).
- priority (string, optional): "normal" | "high" | "background".
- fallback_policy (string, optional): "model_variant,region,delay" (comma-separated prioritized fallback types).

Note: the schema is intentionally permissive for optional fields. Clients should always set protocol_version and client_request_id.

Capability negotiation (handshake)
- Clients send protocol_version and client_capabilities (list of short tokens). Example clients_capabilities: ["streaming-v2","structured-output-v1","quantized-exec"]
- The runtime responds (synchronously in the initial response or in headers for streaming) with server_capabilities and accepted_protocol_version plus reason codes for features not accepted.
- Example minimal negotiation exchange (pseudo):
  - Client: {protocol_version: "rapi/1.2", client_capabilities: ["streaming-v2","quantized-exec"]} 
  - Server: {accepted_protocol_version: "rapi/1.2", server_capabilities: ["streaming-v1","quantized-exec"], feature_downgrade: ["streaming-v2->streaming-v1"]}
- Negotiation failure: server may return ERROR code 6001 (NEGOTIATION_FAILED) with a short human message and structured list of missing required capabilities. Clients should treat negotiation failure as a terminal error for that policy and either retry with fewer requirements or fall back to another runtime.

Compatibility guarantees
- Backward compatibility: fields in the core schema once added are supported as inputs by all future accepted_protocol_version tokens for a minimum deprecation window of 90 days after public announcement.
- Additive extensions: servers may add new optional fields without breaking clients. New fields are considered additive and clients must ignore unrecognized fields.
- Safe removal: a field may be deprecated and removed only after: 1) announcement in release notes and changelog, 2) 90 days minimum, 3) runtime responds with explicit deprecation metadata in negotiation (deprecation_date, replacement_hint).
- Servers guarantee: if accepted_protocol_version == client.protocol_version, request semantics are stable per contract. If the runtime accepts a lower protocol_version, clients must expect possible feature downgrades and explicit downgrade reasons.

Error code taxonomy (machine-readable codes + handling guidance)
- 1000 INVALID_REQUEST_SCHEMA: request failed validation (missing required core field). Client should fix and retry.
- 1001 MALFORMED_INPUT: inputs violate type constraints (e.g., chat where text expected). Client fix required.
- 2000 MODEL_NOT_FOUND: model id unknown. Try catalog lookup or use fallback model.
- 2001 MODEL_VERSION_MISMATCH: requested version unavailable; response may include compatible_version_hint. Client may retry with suggested version.
- 3000 CAPACITY_EXCEEDED: runtime at capacity for desired tier. Retry with exponential backoff; if urgent, consult fallback_policy.
- 3001 QUEUE_TIMEOUT: request expired in queue. Client may retry or lower batch window/priority.
- 4000 KERNEL_MISMATCH: runtime has no kernel that satisfies kernel_hint + model (e.g. quantized kernel missing). Suggested actions: retry without kernel_hint or allow fallback.
- 4001 KERNEL_EXEC_FAILURE: kernel crashed during execution. Runtime will attempt automatic fallback. Client should treat as transient and retry idempotently.
- 4002 KV_CACHE_CORRUPTION: cache returned data that failed verification. Runtime will drop cache entry and may retry core compute. Clients get this only if they set cache_affinity strict.
- 5000 INTERNAL_RUNTIME_ERROR: generic server failure; treat as transient. No guarantees about partial outputs.
- 6000 NEGOTIATION_FAILED: capability negotiation could not satisfy required features. Client should either relax requirements or route to an alternate runtime.
- 7000 STREAM_INTERRUPTED: streaming connection was cut (network or server). Client should reconnect and resume if possible.

Each error response must include: error_code (int), error_name (short token), human_message (string), retryable (boolean), suggested_actions (array-of-strings). Runtimes should include best-effort structured hints to automate fallbacks.

Idempotency and retries
- client_request_id is the primary idempotency key. Servers should attempt idempotent dedupe for 24 hours for generation requests.
- For non-idempotent flows (e.g., streaming partial tokens), clients should use the same client_request_id and server-provided resume tokens when supported.

KV cache contract and failure modes
- Cache keys: deterministic by (model, model_version, input_fingerprint, cache_policy). Clients may provide cache_affinity (allowing strong affinity to read cached prefixes) but this is advisory.
- Cache TTL: runtime supplies cache_ttl_hint to indicate expected freshness; clients should treat it as best-effort.
- Populate-only mode: when kv_cache_policy=="populate_only", runtime will not use cached values to short-circuit execution but will write entries after compute. Good for privacy-sensitive requests.
- Cache verification: runtime may attach cache_proof field (short hash) for strong verification in environments configured with KMS-backed signing.
- Failure signals: 4002 KV_CACHE_CORRUPTION, 3002 CACHE_MISS (informational, not an error).

Kernel selection and execution hints
- kernel_hint is advisory only. Valid values: prefer_fast_fp16, prefer_quantized_int8, prefer_low_memory, prefer_cpu_fallback.
- Runtimes may select a different kernel than requested but must:
  1) include kernel_used token in response metadata,
  2) set kernel_changed boolean if they deviated from kernel_hint,
  3) if deviation could change output semantics (rare), return WARNING code 8001 SEMANTIC_VARIANT with explanation.
- Kernel-level regressions: server should map kernel failures to KERNEL_EXEC_FAILURE (4001) and attempt automatic fallback to a more general kernel.

Scheduling semantics
- Best-effort scheduling: runtime exposes three priority classes (background, normal, high) used to influence queue ordering and preemption. Not a hard SLA unless configured on Dedicated plans.
- Batching: batching_hint_ms provides a request-level preference for coalescing. Server may ignore large values when latency_slo_ms is small.
- Preemption and fairness: high-priority requests may preempt queued background work; background may be delayed without guarantee.

Response metadata (recommended fields in every successful response)
- server_request_id (string)
- accepted_protocol_version (string)
- server_capabilities (list of tokens)
- kernel_used (token)
- cache_hit (boolean)
- cache_ttl_hint (int seconds)
- processing_time_ms (int)
- model_version_served (string)

Sample request + server reply (short)
- Client request: {client_request_id: "u-123", protocol_version: "rapi/1.2", model: "redwood-v1", kernel_hint: "prefer_quantized_int8", input_type: "text", input: "Summarize the following..."}  
- Server reply (200): {server_request_id: "s-987", accepted_protocol_version: "rapi/1.2", server_capabilities: ["quantized-exec","streaming-v1"], kernel_used: "quant-int8-v2", cache_hit: false, model_version_served: "redwood-v1@2025-11-01"}  

Graceful degradation patterns (recommended client behavior)
1) If error_code == 3000 CAPACITY_EXCEEDED: retry to same region with exponential backoff up to N attempts, then switch to cheaper model if fallback_policy includes model_variant.
2) If error_code == 4000 KERNEL_MISMATCH: retry without kernel_hint or with kernel_hint changed to prefer_fast_fp16.
3) If error_code == 6000 NEGOTIATION_FAILED: request short list of server_capabilities and reattempt after relaxing required features.

Observability & debugging hints
- Include negotiation events in request traces.
- Surface server_capabilities and accepted_protocol_version in logs for correlation.
- Error events should include a small, stable error token for automated routing (e.g., KERNEL_EXEC_FAILURE).

Security and privacy considerations
- When cache_affinity or cache_proof is used, ensure no sensitive user PII is stored without explicit policy. Provide a populate_only escape hatch.
- Negotiation step must never leak other tenants’ capability lists; only announce capabilities applicable to the current runtime and tenant.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Protocol naming: semver-like tokens vs date-based (e.g. rapi/2025-11). Date-based simpler for deprecation windows but semver easier for feature ranges.
- Deletion window length: 90 days is a balance; consider 180 days for enterprise stability.
- How aggressive should automatic kernel fallbacks be before surfacing warnings to clients?

Next steps
- Engineering: implement negotiation headers + accepted_protocol_version in a feature branch (owner: Miguel).
- Product: finalize deprecation policy and publish changelog template (owner: Priya).
- SRE: add traces for negotiation and kernel_used metadata (owner: Owen).
- Ship a beta with SDK clients that automatically surface downgrade reasons and helper utilities for fallbacks.

Appendix: short checklist for runtime implementers
- [ ] Validate presence of client_request_id and protocol_version.
- [ ] Return accepted_protocol_version and server_capabilities in metadata.
- [ ] Include kernel_used and kernel_changed when relevant.
- [ ] Return machine-readable error_code + suggested_actions on failures.
- [ ] Maintain deprecation changelog and emit deprecation metadata in negotiation.

Document history

- 2025-11-18 internal review (Miguel, Priya)
